land.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

predecessors.note: Argos and Nauplia were 'the centre of a domain under Leo Sgouros' in the first years of the 13th century; Sgouros died in 1208 and his men held the citadels until the Franks took Nauplia and then Argos in 1212. No dossier exists for the Sgouros domain (c.1201-1210).

successors.note: Maria of Enghien sold the lordship to Venice on 12 December 1388 for an annual subsidy of 700 ducats; Venice 'quickly ousted Nerio from Nauplia'. Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi stayed with Theodore Palaiologos until 11 June 1394, when he ceded them to Venice.
Despot Theodore Palaiologos took Argos in 1388 'with Nerio Acciaioli and an Ottoman army'. Infobox 'Succeeded by: Despotate of the Morea; Republic of Venice'.

rulers.name: Walter VI of Brienne
rulers.title: lord, Duke of Athens
rulers.note: Largely absent from Greece; his 1331 attempt to retake Athens failed; died at Poitiers in 1356. The lordship had been held by the de la Roche and the Brienne dukes of Athens since 1212.

rulers.name: Maria of Enghien
rulers.title: lady
rulers.note: Underage in 1376 (her uncle Louis governed for her); married the Venetian Pietro Cornaro in May 1377; sold the lordship to Venice on 12 December 1388.

correction.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria draws Argos and Nauplia with Athens in 1216-1271 and with Achaea otherwise). The Argolid around Nauplia and Argos, a fief of the Principality of Achaea held by the Dukes of Athens: 'granted as a fief to Otto de la Roche' in 1212. The page gives no area; the 25 km radius is an upper bound for the plain.

region.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

ledger.note: 1212: the Franks take Argos and Nauplia and grant them to Otto de la Roche. After Acrocorinth fell in 1210 the Franks took Nauplia 'and finally Argos in 1212'; 'Geoffrey I of Villehardouin granted the two cities to Otto de la Roche as a fief' with 400 hyperpyra of income from Corinth. Nauplia's date is not given. Sgouros had died in 1208 and his men held the citadels.

1356: the lordship passes to Guy of Enghien. After Walter of Brienne's death at Poitiers in 1356 'the lordship was inherited by Guy of Enghien'; the Brienne and de la Roche had held it as Dukes of Athens, even after the Catalans took Athens in 1311.
May 1377: Maria of Enghien marries the Venetian Pietro Cornaro. Maria inherited after her father's death shortly after October 1376; her uncle Louis governed for her while she was underage.

1388: Despot Theodore Palaiologos seizes Argos. 'Despot Theodore Palaiologos took Argos with Nerio Acciaioli and an Ottoman army'; 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394'. The Nerio Acciaioli page: Theodore occupied Argos; Nerio seized Nauplia.
12 December 1388: Maria of Enghien sells Nauplia to Venice. She 'sold them to Venice on 12 December in exchange for an annual subsidy of 700' ducats; 'Venice quickly ousted Nerio from Nauplia'.

region.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

ledger.note: 12 December 1388: the Lordship of Argos and Nauplia ends. Infobox 'Sold to Venice: 1388'; Argos itself had been taken by Theodore Palaiologos.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Argos and Nauplia

zones.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

wars.outcome: After the fall of Acrocorinth in 1210 the Franks under Geoffrey I of Villehardouin took Nauplia and then Argos in 1212 from Sgouros's men and granted them to Otto de la Roche.
wars.note: The page gives no date for Nauplia; Boniface of Montferrat died in 1207 and Sgouros in 1208.

wars.name: Contest for Argos and Nauplia after the sale

zones.text: Argos and Nauplia and the Argolid plain

wars.outcome: Theodore Palaiologos took Argos with Nerio Acciaioli and an Ottoman army in 1388; Nerio took Nauplia but Venice ousted him; Venice kept Nauplia and received Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi from Theodore on 11 June 1394.

certainty.note: A fief around two fortified towns; no page gives its limits.

sources.title: Lordship of Argos and Nauplia
sources.note: Infobox (capital, 1212, 1388), Sgouros, Frankish conquest 1210-1212, the Brienne and Enghien, 1377, the sale of 12 December 1388, Theodore's Argos to 11 June 1394. No area.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row of its own (it draws Argos and Nauplia with Athens in 1216-1271 and with Achaea otherwise). Slug is the one eu-05-c and eu-05-d proposed. Only one page opened (the budget for a state with no Cliopatria shape is 2; the Lordship page covers the whole life). Not settled: (1) the Sgouros domain (c.1201-1208/10: Corinth, Boeotia and Thessaly) is a separate warlord realm that needs its own dossier ('leo-sgouros'); (2) the holders between Otto de la Roche (1212) and Walter of Brienne (1311) are not on the page, so the ruler strip starts in 1311; (3) the lordship was a fief of the Principality of Achaea (the suzerain's dossier carries the vassal events); (4) Nauplia's exact conquest date; (5) no area.
